Comment: Order saga: reserve inventory, request payment from the provider and PAUSE until its signed webhook resumes the saga (task token, 120 s timeout), then BEGIN FULFILLMENT (the point after which the customer can no longer cancel) and fulfil each order line on its own (inline Map). All lines delivered: COMPLETED. Some lines unavailable: refund just those lines, write them off, PARTIALLY_FULFILLED. None: refund and write off everything, FAILED. If payment fails or times out it compensates in reverse order: refund through the provider, release the stock, mark the order FAILED with a reason. CUSTOMER CANCELLATION (until fulfillment starts): the cancel API fails the payment wait with OrderCancelled, or BeginFulfillment finds the cancel; both go to the cancel branch: void the payment and refund what is left, release the stock, CANCELLED. A failing order that the customer cancelled meanwhile also ends CANCELLED. Every outcome notifies the customer.

ReserveInventory.Comment: Lambda order-saga-reserve-inventory: decrements stock for every item in ONE DynamoDB transaction (all or nothing) and marks the order RESERVED. Throws OutOfStock if any item is short. Passes cancellable=true, so the order is stamped as running on a definition with a cancel branch (step 2.4).

RequestPayment.Comment: Lambda order-saga-request-payment stores THIS task token on payment intent PI-<orderId> and asks DemoPay to charge (SQS, 2-5 s). The saga then waits: payment_webhook calls SendTaskSuccess (paid) or SendTaskFailure PaymentDeclined. No callback within 120 s -> States.Timeout -> MarkPaymentTimedOut. PaymentTransientError (payment_flaky) is retried 2 s, 4 s, 8 s; each retry gets a new token. OrderCancelled (the customer cancelled: SendTaskFailure from the cancel API, or request_payment refusing a cancelled order) is caught separately and goes to the cancel branch.

MarkPaymentTimedOut.Comment: Direct DynamoDB UpdateItem (no Lambda): payment intent REQUESTED -> TIMED_OUT, ONLY if still REQUESTED. If the webhook captured the payment a moment earlier (SUCCEEDED), the condition fails and the saga continues to RefundPayment, which refunds it.

DescribeTimeout.Comment: Replaces the raw States.Timeout error with a readable one, so the order's failureReason says 'payment timeout'.

Result.Cause: payment timeout - DemoPay did not confirm the payment within 120 s

WarehouseSpeed.Comment: DEMO ONLY: simulate=fulfillment_slow waits 10 s before the warehouse starts (time to cancel a paid order). Every other order goes straight on.

WaitBeforeFulfillment.Comment: DEMO ONLY (fulfillment_slow): the order is paid and still cancellable for these 10 s.

BeginFulfillment.Comment: Lambda order-saga-begin-fulfillment: ONE conditional write PAYMENT_CAPTURED -> FULFILLING, only if the customer has not cancelled. Returns outcome FULFILLING (from now on a cancel gets 409) or CANCEL_REQUESTED (the customer won: cancel branch). Retries, no Catch: on a real failure the execution fails loudly (alarm order-saga-cancellation-errors) and can be redriven.

CancelledBeforeFulfillment.Comment: The customer cancelled after paying but before the warehouse started -> refund everything (cancel branch). Otherwise fulfil (fulfillment_slow first waits 10 s more while FULFILLING, so a late cancel gets 409).

WaitWhilePacking.Comment: DEMO ONLY (fulfillment_slow): FULFILLING for 10 s, so a cancel now is rejected with 409 TOO_LATE_TO_CANCEL.

FulfillItems.Comment: Inline Map, one iteration per order line (up to 5 at once): Lambda order-saga-fulfill-item picks the line (reserved -> sold). Each iteration catches its OWN errors and returns {lineId, status: FULFILLED | UNAVAILABLE, reason}, so one damaged item can never fail the whole Map or the order. Runs only after the payment succeeded; reservation before it stays all-or-nothing.

FulfillItem.Comment: Lambda order-saga-fulfill-item: ONE line, idempotent (a retry never moves stock twice). FulfillmentTransientError (transaction conflicts) is retried; ItemUnavailable is not.

LineUnavailable.Comment: This line could not be fulfilled: report it (with the reason) instead of failing the Map.

SummarizeFulfillment.Comment: Counts the Map's results: how many lines were fulfilled, which were unavailable and why.

FulfillmentOutcome.Comment: All lines delivered -> COMPLETED as before. No line delivered -> refund and write off all, FAILED. Otherwise -> partial refund, PARTIALLY_FULFILLED.

PartialRefund.Comment: Lambda order-saga-refund-payment (lineIds mode): refunds ONLY the unavailable lines, each at the amount stored on the order when it was created. DemoPay refunds each line at most once and never above the charge (I7). No Catch on purpose: after its retries the execution FAILS here (alarm order-saga-refund-or-write-off-errors) and is REDRIVEN from this state once fixed; it is idempotent per line.

WriteOffLines.Comment: Lambda order-saga-write-off-lines: the unavailable lines' units go reserved -> writtenOff (NOT back on sale), with an audit record in order-saga-write-offs. No Catch on purpose: after its retries the execution FAILS here (alarm order-saga-refund-or-write-off-errors) and is REDRIVEN from this state once fixed; it is idempotent per line.

MarkOrderPartiallyFulfilled.Comment: Direct DynamoDB UpdateItem (no Lambda): status PARTIALLY_FULFILLED, appended to statusHistory with what was delivered and refunded.

detail.S.$: States.Format('{} of {} items delivered - {} {} refunded for the unavailable items', $.fulfillment.fulfilledCount, $.fulfillment.lineCount, $.order.currency, $.lineRefund.refundedAmount)

NotifyCustomerPartial.Comment: Direct SNS Publish integration (no Lambda): tells the customer what was delivered, which items were refunded and how much.

OrderPartiallyFulfilled.Comment: Saga finished: the available lines were delivered, the unavailable ones refunded and written off, the customer notified.

RefundAllLines.Comment: Every line was unavailable: refunds every line (together, the whole charge: the intent becomes REFUNDED), through the same idempotent, capped line refunds. No Catch on purpose: after its retries the execution FAILS here (alarm order-saga-refund-or-write-off-errors) and is REDRIVEN from this state once fixed; it is idempotent per line.

WriteOffAllLines.Comment: Every line's units go reserved -> writtenOff, with audit records. No Catch on purpose: after its retries the execution FAILS here (alarm order-saga-refund-or-write-off-errors) and is REDRIVEN from this state once fixed; it is idempotent per line.

DescribeAllUnavailable.Comment: Sets error AllItemsUnavailable and a readable failureReason, then joins the normal failure path (MarkOrderFailed, notify).
DescribeAllUnavailable.Output: {% $merge([$states.input, {'error': {'Error': 'AllItemsUnavailable', 'Cause': 'all items unavailable'}, 'failureReason': 'AllItemsUnavailable: all items unavailable - ' & $states.input.order.currency & ' ' & $states.input.lineRefund.refundedAmount & ' refunded to your DemoPay wallet and every line written off'}]) %}

MarkOrderCompleted.Comment: Direct DynamoDB UpdateItem integration (no Lambda): sets status COMPLETED and appends it to statusHistory. Reached only after the webhook confirmed the payment (SendTaskSuccess).

NotifyCustomer.Comment: Direct SNS Publish integration (no Lambda): emails the order confirmation via the order-saga-notifications topic.

OrderCompleted.Comment: Saga finished successfully: stock reserved, payment captured, order COMPLETED, customer notified.

RefundPayment.Comment: COMPENSATION - Lambda order-saga-refund-payment: refunds any charge for this order through DemoPay's idempotent refund API (a no-op if nothing was charged) and marks the intent REFUNDED. An intent still REQUESTED is marked FAILED (abandoned), so a later charge is refunded by the webhook.

ReleaseInventory.Comment: COMPENSATION - Lambda order-saga-release-inventory: gives back exactly the stock this order reserved. Idempotent, so retries can never double-release.

DescribeFailure.Comment: Builds a readable failureReason such as 'PaymentDeclined: Card declined by issuer (simulated)' from the caught error. A Lambda error's Cause is a JSON string, so its errorMessage is extracted.

CheckCancelBeforeFailing.Comment: Direct DynamoDB GetItem (no Lambda): did the customer cancel while this order was failing (e.g. the 120 s payment timeout fired just as they cancelled, so SendTaskFailure found the token already closed)? A cancel the API accepted (202) must end CANCELLED, not FAILED.

CancelledWhileFailing.Comment: cancelRequestedAt present -> the cancel branch (every step is idempotent, so what compensation already did is a no-op: the void still stops a late charge). Otherwise FAILED as before.

MarkOrderFailed.Comment: Direct DynamoDB UpdateItem integration (no Lambda): sets status FAILED and failureReason, and appends FAILED to statusHistory.

NotifyCustomerFailure.Comment: Direct SNS Publish integration (no Lambda): tells the customer the order FAILED, why, and that any payment was refunded.

Parameters.Message.$:
States.Format('Hello,

Unfortunately your order {} could not be completed.

Reason: {}

Any payment taken has been refunded to your DemoPay wallet.

Sorry for the inconvenience - Order Saga.', $.orderId, $.failureReason)

OrderFailed.Comment: Saga ended in failure after compensation. The execution shows as FAILED in the console, with the reason as its Cause.

RefundWhatIsLeft.Comment: CANCEL BRANCH - Lambda order-saga-refund-payment (cancelled mode): voids the payment intent at DemoPay (a charge still queued there takes nothing), then refunds whatever is left of a charge that did happen (once, never above the charge: I7). A no-op when nothing was charged. Retries, no Catch: a failure stops the execution (alarm order-saga-refund-or-write-off-errors) and it is redriven from here.

CancelReleaseInventory.Comment: CANCEL BRANCH - Lambda order-saga-release-inventory: every reserved unit back to available stock, exactly once (idempotent; a checkout hold was consumed at reservation, so its expiry can't release it again). Retries, no Catch (alarm order-saga-cancellation-errors, then redrive).

DescribeCancellation.Comment: Builds the history detail and the email line: 'refunded INR X' or 'nothing was charged'.
DescribeCancellation.Output: {% ( $amount := $number($states.input.cancelRefund.refundedAmount); $money := $states.input.order.currency & ' ' & $states.input.cancelRefund.refundedAmount; $merge([$states.input, {'cancellation': $amount > 0 ? {'detail': 'Cancelled by the customer - ' & $money & ' refunded to the DemoPay wallet', 'emailLine': 'We refunded ' & $money & ' to your DemoPay wallet.'} : {'detail': 'Cancelled by the customer - nothing was charged', 'emailLine': 'Nothing was charged. If a payment was still being processed, it is refunded to your DemoPay wallet automatically.'}}]) ) %}

MarkOrderCancelled.Comment: Direct DynamoDB UpdateItem (no Lambda): status CANCELLED (terminal, distinct from FAILED), cancelledAt, and CANCELLED appended to statusHistory with what was refunded.

NotifyCustomerCancelled.Comment: Direct SNS Publish integration (no Lambda): tells the customer the order was cancelled and what was refunded.

Parameters.Message.$:
States.Format('Hi {},

Your order {} has been cancelled, as you asked.

Items:
{}

{}

The items are back in stock for other customers.

Order Saga.', $.order.customerName, $.orderId, $.order.itemsSummary, $.cancellation.emailLine)

OrderCancelled.Comment: Saga finished: cancelled by the customer before fulfillment, nothing kept from the payment, stock back, customer notified.
